title: compatibility lifecycle helix and deployment safeguards
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As Redwood supports multiple release lanes (fast, stable, longevity) we lack a compact, testable artifact that describes cross-surface compatibility guarantees, automated upgrade checks, and the automated gating framework for staged rollouts. This ticket builds a single source artifact (the 'compatibility helix') and associated deployment safeguards so runtime, API, SDKs, and Console teams can reason about safe upgrades and automated validation.

Goals: 1) Define a compact compatibility helix that maps semantic compatibility levels to runtime binary, API schema, SDK surface, and console migration actions. 2) Produce a machine-readable matrix that CI can validate at PR time. 3) Implement rollout gate definitions (smoke, canary, cohort, full) and corresponding automated checks and rollback hooks. 4) Deliver a migration playbook and sample upgrade job that demonstrates runtime->API->SDK->Console coordinated rollout.

Non-goals: This ticket does not ship the full rollout automation for Dedicated clusters or on-prem upgrade orchestrator; it focuses on the compatibility artifact, gating taxonomy, and CI-time validators for hosted and Dedicated pilot paths.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility helix document published in Confluence with mappings for runtime, API, SDK, console
Machine-readable compatibility matrix (YAML) added to release-infra repo and validated by unit tests
CI validation job fails PRs that declare incompatible changes without an agreed mitigation plan
Rollout gate definitions added to rollout service and wired to canary pipeline with smoke tests
Playbook with step-by-step rollback instructions and postmortem checklist authored and reviewed
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design and review the compatibility helix with runtime, api, sdk, console owners (2 sprints). Phase 2: Author a YAML schema and reference implementation that CI can import; add unit tests and sample validators. Phase 3: Implement rollout gate primitives in rollout service and wire a canary pipeline that enforces gates for the sample runtime release. Phase 4: Run a dry-run upgrade with a non-customer demo cluster and update playbook from findings. Phase 5: Hand off to release engineering and docs for org-wide adoption.
rollout_gates: smoke: basic health + API handshake tests
canary: 1% traffic cohort with KV cache compatibility validation
cohort: progressive 10/25/50 cohorts with runtime metrics thresholds
full: automated acceptance criteria + manual approval for major incompatible changes
compatibility_matrix_summary: The helix encodes compatibility at three levels: compatible (no action), compatible-with-migrations (requires non-breaking SDK shim or Console mapping), and incompatible-with-blocker (requires coordination and migration plan). For each surface we record: minimal supported partner versions, required feature flags, data-migration steps (if any), suggested quantization/kernel fallbacks, and regression test sets.
